description: Phase 3 (v2) — orchestration workflow matched to the REAL backend. Flow: webhook entry → validate input (secret + SSRF guard) → POST /api/v1/jobs (backend persists job + 15 stages and enqueues on BullMQ; the worker runs all stages internally) → poll GET /api/v1/jobs/:id until a terminal state → respond with download URL / review notice / failure. n8n owns job lifecycle; the backend worker owns the 15 pipeline stages. Import into n8n; required env: BACKEND_URL, N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
name: product-video-main

nodes.name: webhook-entry
nodes.notes: Entry point. POST { productUrl, durationSeconds?, language?, voice?, visualStyle?, platform?, idempotencyKey? } with header x-n8n-secret. Auth is verified in validate-input against $env.N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET (no n8n credential needed).

nodes.name: validate-input
nodes.notes: STAGE 1 (url_validation): verify x-n8n-secret, validate productUrl is public http(s) (SSRF guard), apply defaults. Throws → error workflow.

nodes.name: create-job
nodes.notes: POST /api/v1/jobs — backend validates (incl. SSRF guard), persists Job + 15 JobStage rows, enqueues on BullMQ. Returns { ok, data: { id, ... } }.

nodes.name: check-created
nodes.notes: True: job created → start polling. False: backend rejected → fail fast.

nodes.name: fail-create
nodes.notes: Builds the job-creation failure payload.

parameters.jsCode:
const r = $input.first().json;
return [{ json: { ok: false, error: 'Job creation failed', detail: r.message ?? r.code ?? 'Backend rejected the request' } }];

nodes.name: respond-create-failed
nodes.notes: Returns HTTP 500 to the caller.

nodes.name: init-poll
nodes.notes: Seeds the poll loop: jobId + attempt counter (max 120 attempts × 20s ≈ 40 min).

parameters.jsCode:
const data = $input.first().json.data;
return [{ json: { jobId: data.id, attempts: 0 } }];

nodes.name: get-status
nodes.notes: GET /api/v1/jobs/:id — job status + 15 stage states + recent events. The backend worker updates stages itself.

nodes.name: normalize-status
nodes.notes: Carries jobId forward (HTTP node replaces item data) and bumps the attempt counter.

nodes.name: is-done
nodes.notes: True: terminal state (COMPLETED / FAILED / CANCELLED / WAITING_FOR_REVIEW) → route. False: keep polling.

nodes.name: within-limit
nodes.notes: True (attempts ≤ 120): wait and poll again. False: give up waiting (job may still run; caller can poll manually).

nodes.name: wait-poll
nodes.notes: Wait 20s between polls. Loops back to get-status.

nodes.name: build-timeout
nodes.notes: Builds the poll-timeout payload (HTTP 504).

parameters.jsCode:
const j = $input.first().json;
return [{ json: { ok: false, jobId: j.jobId, status: j.status, error: 'Timed out waiting for job completion (40 min). The job may still be running — check it with GET /api/v1/jobs/' + j.jobId } }];

nodes.name: respond-timeout
nodes.notes: Returns HTTP 504 to the caller.

nodes.name: is-completed
nodes.notes: True: COMPLETED → deliver. False: check review state.

nodes.name: is-review
nodes.notes: True: WAITING_FOR_REVIEW → human approval via dashboard. False: FAILED/CANCELLED → failure response.

nodes.name: build-success
nodes.notes: Builds the success payload: jobId, download URL, result URL, per-stage states.

nodes.name: respond-success
nodes.notes: Returns HTTP 200 with the download URL to the caller.

nodes.name: build-review
nodes.notes: Builds the human-review payload.

nodes.name: respond-review
nodes.notes: Returns HTTP 200 (review pending) to the caller.

nodes.name: build-failed
nodes.notes: Builds the job-failure payload from the backend's error message.

parameters.jsCode:
const j = $input.first().json;
return [{ json: { ok: false, jobId: j.jobId, status: j.status, error: (j.job && (j.job.errorMessage || j.job.lastError)) || 'Job failed. Check the dashboard for details.' } }];

nodes.name: respond-failed
nodes.notes: Returns HTTP 500 to the caller.
